claim: Drosophila larvae employ their visual system for navigation, entrainment of circadian rhythms, formation of associative memories, and may respond to the presence of other larvae.
source: Larvae of the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster employ their visual system for a range of diverse behaviors including navigation, entrainment of circadian rhythms, formation of associative memories and may respond to the presence of other larvae (Kane et al., 2013; Humberg and Sprecher, 2017; Slepian et al., 2015; Justice et al., 2012; Yamanaka et al., 2013; von Essen et al., 2011; Gong, 2009; Mazzoni et al., 2005; Gerber et al., 2004; Sawin-McCormack et al., 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research studies.

claim: The simple eyes of the Drosophila larva (Bolwig Organ) consist of only about 12 photoreceptor neurons each.
source: The simple eyes of the larva (also termed Bolwig Organ, BO) consist of only about 12 PRs each and yet drive a wide range of behaviors, raising questions on the organizational logic of the underlying visual circuit.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the manuscript text.

claim: Larval eyes contain two photoreceptor types: one expressing Rhodopsin5 (Rh5) and one expressing Rhodopsin6 (Rh6).
source: Larval eyes contain two PR-types, either expressing the blue-tuned Rhodopsin5 (Rh5) or the green-tuned Rhodopsin6 (Rh6) (Malpel et al., 2002; Hassan et al., 2005; Rodriguez Moncalvo and Campos, 2005; Sprecher et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Rh5 is blue-tuned and Rh6 is green-tuned.
source: Larval eyes contain two PR-types, either expressing the blue-tuned Rhodopsin5 (Rh5) or the green-tuned Rhodopsin6 (Rh6) (Malpel et al., 2002; Hassan et al., 2005; Rodriguez Moncalvo and Campos, 2005; Sprecher et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: For rapid navigation away from light exposure, only the Rh5-PRs seem essential.
source: Interestingly, for rapid navigation away from light exposure only the Rh5-PRs seem essential, whereas to entrain the molecular clock either PR subtype suffices (Keene et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: To entrain the molecular clock, either PR subtype suffices.
source: Interestingly, for rapid navigation away from light exposure only the Rh5-PRs seem essential, whereas to entrain the molecular clock either PR subtype suffices (Keene et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Larval photoreceptors project their axons in a joint nerve (Bolwig nerve) terminating in a small neuropil domain termed the larval optic neuropil (LON).
source: Larval PRs project their axons in a joint nerve (Bolwig nerve) terminating in a small neuropil domain termed the larval optic neuropil (LON).
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the manuscript text.

claim: Previous studies identified eleven neurons innervating the LON in each brain hemisphere.
source: Previous studies identified eleven neurons innervating the LON in each brain hemisphere. This includes four lateral neurons (LaNs) expressing the pigment dispersing factor (Pdf) neuropeptide (Pdf-LaNs) and a fifth non-Pdf-expressing LaN (5th-LaN), all being part of the clock circuit (Kaneko et al., 1997), as well as a serotonergic neuron and three optic lobe pioneer cells (OLPs) (Helfrich-Förster, 1997; Rodriguez Moncalvo and Campos, 2005; 2009; Tix et al., 1989).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Two unpaired median octopaminergic/tyraminergic neurons extend neurites into the larval optic neuropils.
source: Recently, two unpaired median octopaminergic/tyraminergic neurons were described to extend neurites into these neuropils (Selcho et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Photoreceptor axons form large globular boutons with polyadic synapses.
source: In a recent study we started to investigate the anatomy of the LON using serial-section transmission electron microscopy (ssTEM) showing that PRs' axons form large globular boutons with polyadic synapses and that the OLPs were parts of their direct targets (Sprecher et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The OLPs are direct targets of photoreceptor neurons.
source: In a recent study we started to investigate the anatomy of the LON using serial-section transmission electron microscopy (ssTEM) showing that PRs' axons form large globular boutons with polyadic synapses and that the OLPs were parts of their direct targets (Sprecher et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The authors mapped the synaptic wiring diagram of the LON by reconstructing all its innervating neurons from a ssTEM volume of a whole first instar larval central nervous system.
source: Here, we mapped the synaptic wiring diagram of the LON by reconstructing all its innervating neurons from a new ssTEM volume of a whole first instar larval central nervous system (Ohyama et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the manuscript text and references the dataset used.

claim: Per hemisphere, there are eleven second order interneurons, two third-order interneurons, and one serotonergic neuron innervating the LON.
source: We found per hemisphere eleven second order interneurons, two third-order interneurons and one serotonergic neuron innervating the LON, plus two unpaired octopaminergic/tyraminergic neurons contacting both hemispheres.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the manuscript text based on the reconstruction.

claim: Two unpaired octopaminergic/tyraminergic neurons contact both hemispheres.
source: We found per hemisphere eleven second order interneurons, two third-order interneurons and one serotonergic neuron innervating the LON, plus two unpaired octopaminergic/tyraminergic neurons contacting both hemispheres.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the manuscript text based on the reconstruction.

claim: The two PR subtypes connect onto distinct subsets of interneurons, showing separation of light signal flow at the first synapse level.
source: We highlighted the separation of light signal flow at the first synapse level as the two PR subtypes connect onto distinct subsets of interneurons.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the manuscript text based on the connectivity analysis.

claim: The resulting circuits may encode both ambient light intensity information and information about the changes of light intensity.
source: Network analysis suggests that the resulting circuits may encode both ambient light intensity information and information about the changes of light intensity.
evidence: The claim is based on network analysis of the connectivity data.

claim: The stratified structure of the larval optic neuropil suggests common organizational principles with the adult fly and vertebrate visual systems.
source: The stratified structure of the larval optic neuropil (LON) suggests common organizational principles with the adult fly and vertebrate visual systems.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the manuscript abstract.

claim: Axonal projections of larval photoreceptor neurons enter the brain lobes ventro-laterally via the Bolwig nerve.
source: Axonal projections of larval photoreceptor neurons (PRs) enter the brain lobes ventro-laterally via the Bolwig nerve and terminate in a small neuropil domain, termed larval optic neuropil (LON; Figure 1A,B, Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1A,B.

claim: Visual interneurons innervate the LON from the central brain through the central optic tract.
source: Visual interneurons innervate the LON from the central brain through the central optic tract (Sprecher et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The authors reconstructed the axon terminals of all PRs and all their synaptic partners from a ssTEM volume.
source: We reconstructed the axon terminals of all PRs and all their synaptic partners, as well as additional LON-innervating neurons that do not form synapses with PRs, from a serial-section transmission electron microscopy (ssTEM) volume spanning the complete central nervous system of a Drosophila first instar larva (using the Collaborative Annotation Toolkit for Massive Amounts of Image Data (CATMAID), Saalfeld et al. (2009); Ohyama et al. (2015); Schneider-Mizell et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the manuscript text.

claim: One lOLP is cholinergic (cha-lOLP) while the other is glutamatergic (glu-lOLP).
source: We found that one lOLP is cholinergic (cha-lOLP) while the other is glutamatergic (glu-lOLP), in agreement with previous studies (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; Yasuyama et al., 1995; Daniels et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and citations.

claim: All VPNs except the four peptidergic Pdf-LaNs are cholinergic.
source: All these VPNs, except the four peptidergic Pdf-LaNs, are cholinergic (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The VPLN is glutamatergic.
source: We found that the VPLN is glutamatergic (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The LON can be subdivided into three distinct layers based on the innervation of the PR subtypes.
source: In Drosophila larvae, the LON can be subdivided into three distinct layers based on the innervation of the PR subtypes, which allows to distinguish them in the ssTEM dataset (Sprecher et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: Rhodopsin6-PRs (Rh6-PRs) terminate in the distal, most outer layer of the LON (LONd).
source: Briefly, Rhodopsin6-PRs (Rh6-PRs) terminate in the distal, most outer layer of the LON (LONd), whereas Rhodopsin5-PRs (Rh5-PRs) terminate in the intermediate LON layer (LONi).
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the manuscript text.

claim: Rhodopsin5-PRs (Rh5-PRs) terminate in the intermediate LON layer (LONi).
source: Briefly, Rhodopsin6-PRs (Rh6-PRs) terminate in the distal, most outer layer of the LON (LONd), whereas Rhodopsin5-PRs (Rh5-PRs) terminate in the intermediate LON layer (LONi).
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the manuscript text.

claim: The most proximal, inner layer of the LON (LONp) lacks direct PRs input.
source: The most proximal, inner layer of the LON (LONp) lacks direct PRs input (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A-C.

claim: Most VPNs, whose dendrites do not reach the LONd, receive direct inputs from Rh5-PRs only.
source: Most VPNs, whose dendrites do not reach the LONd, receive direct inputs from Rh5-PRs only, whereas the dendrites of Pdf-LaNs span both the LONd and LONi, integrating inputs from both Rh5- and Rh6-PRs (see below; Figure 1E–K).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1E-K.

claim: The dendrites of Pdf-LaNs span both the LONd and LONi, integrating inputs from both Rh5- and Rh6-PRs.
source: Most VPNs, whose dendrites do not reach the LONd, receive direct inputs from Rh5-PRs only, whereas the dendrites of Pdf-LaNs span both the LONd and LONi, integrating inputs from both Rh5- and Rh6-PRs (see below; Figure 1E–K).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1E-K.

claim: The absence of PRs' axon terminals in the LONp deprives the third-order interneurons, VPLN and Tiny VLN, from any direct PRs inputs.
source: The absence of PRs' axon terminals in the LONp deprives the third-order interneurons, VPLN and Tiny VLN, whose dendrites are restricted to the LONp, from any direct PRs inputs (Figures 1K and 2F).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figures 1K and 2F.

claim: VPNs' axons target three distinct protocerebral areas: the superior lateral protocerebrum, the lateral inferior protocerebrum and the ventro lateral protocerebrum.
source: Beyond the LON, VPNs' axons target three distinct protocerebral areas, namely the superior lateral protocerebrum, the lateral inferior protocerebrum and the ventro lateral protocerebrum (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2C,D.

claim: These areas overlap in parts with the lateral horn and the mushroom body calyx.
source: Interestingly, these areas overlap in parts with the lateral horn, involved in innate behaviors, and the mushroom body calyx, involved in associative memory (see below).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on the reconstruction.

claim: Within the LON, the dendrites of VPNs are mainly postsynaptic.
source: Within the LON, the dendrites of VPNs are mainly postsynaptic, whereas their axons, upon reaching higher brain areas, present both presynaptic and postsynaptic sites (Figure 1E–K).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1E-K.

claim: VPNs' axons, upon reaching higher brain areas, present both presynaptic and postsynaptic sites.
source: Within the LON, the dendrites of VPNs are mainly postsynaptic, whereas their axons, upon reaching higher brain areas, present both presynaptic and postsynaptic sites (Figure 1E–K).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1E-K.

claim: VPNs outputs are modulated by input from non-visual neurons.
source: This suggests that VPNs outputs are modulated by input from non-visual neurons, similarly to how olfactory projection interneurons receive non-olfactory inputs (Berck et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the connectivity data and comparison with olfactory system.

claim: pOLP and the VPLN receive up to 30% of their inputs from non-LON neurons.
source: In particular pOLP and the VPLN receive up to 30% of their inputs from non-LON neurons (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2E.

claim: Rh6-PRs synapse principally onto VLNs (79%) and much less onto VPNs (15%, all onto one single VPN type: the Pdf-LaNs).
source: Supporting this notion, we found that Rh6-PRs synapse principally onto VLNs (79%) and much less onto VPNs (15%, all onto one single VPN type: the Pdf-LaNs; Figure 2E, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2E and source data.

claim: Rh5-PRs preferentially synapse onto VPNs (90%) and much less onto VLNs (6%).
source: Conversely, Rh5-PRs preferentially synapse onto VPNs (90%) and much less onto VLNs (6%).
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the manuscript text based on connectivity data.

claim: The four Pdf-LaNs are the only interneurons that receive direct inputs from both Rh6-PRs and Rh5-PRs.
source: An exception to this segregation of PRs inputs are the Pdf-expressing LaNs of the clock circuits. Indeed, the four Pdf-LaNs are the only interneurons that receive direct inputs from both Rh6-PRs and Rh5-PRs (20% from Rh6-PRs and 15% from Rh5-PRs, Figures 2E and 3B), supporting behavioral evidence that either PR-subtype may entrain the larval clock (Keene et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figures 2E and 3B and a citation.

claim: The two lOLPs receive from Rh6-PRs: up to 75% of cha-OLP input and 58% of glu-lOLP input.
source: Rh6-PRs target the two main VLNs of the LON: the cha- and glu-lOLPs (Figures 2E,F and 3A). Furthermore, the lOLPs main inputs come from Rh6-PRs: up to 75% of cha-OLP input and 58% of glu-lOLP input.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figures 2E,F and 3A.

claim: The two VLNs synapse onto most VPNs including the four Pdf-LaNs and the 5th-LaN of the circadian clock, the nc-LaNs, PVL09 and the third-order interneuron VPLN.
source: Importantly, these two VLNs synapse onto most VPNs including the four Pdf-LaNs and the 5th-LaN of the circadian clock, the nc-LaNs, PVL09 and the third-order interneuron VPLN (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3C.

claim: pOLP is the only VPN that does not receive inputs from its sister cells, the two lOLPs.
source: pOLP is the only VPN that does not receive inputs from its sister cells, the two lOLPs, and therefore create a direct output pathway of the Rh5-PRs light dependent information towards higher brain regions (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3B,C.

claim: pOLP is strongly interconnected through axo-axonic connections with PVL09.
source: pOLP is strongly interconnected through axo-axonic connections with PVL09 suggesting that they may reciprocally cross-modulate their synaptic output (Figures 2E and 3C; Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figures 2E and 3C and source data.

claim: The third-order interneuron VPLN does not receive direct inputs from PRs.
source: The third-order interneuron VPLN, which does not receive direct inputs from PRs (Figure 3B), is downstream of the two lOLPs and is itself connecting onto several VPNs including the 5th-LaN, the two nc-LaNs and PVL09 creating another layer of possible computation (see discussion, Figure 3C–E).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3B.

claim: The VPLN is downstream of the two lOLPs and connects onto several VPNs including the 5th-LaN, the two nc-LaNs and PVL09.
source: The third-order interneuron VPLN, which does not receive direct inputs from PRs (Figure 3B), is downstream of the two lOLPs and is itself connecting onto several VPNs including the 5th-LaN, the two nc-LaNs and PVL09 creating another layer of possible computation (see discussion, Figure 3C–E).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3C-E.

claim: pOLP targets the lower lateral horn, an area also innervated by the multiglomerular olfactory projection interneuron (mPN) Seahorse.
source: pOLP targets the lower lateral horn, an area also innervated by the multiglomerular olfactory projection interneuron (mPN) Seahorse (Berck et al., 2016; Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 3) with whom it shares numerous postsynaptic partners (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and a citation.

claim: Three sister VPNs (the 5th-LaN and both nc-LaN 1 and 2) present similar axon trajectories, dropping synapses in the lateral horn until reaching the accessory calyx of the mushroom body.
source: Three sister VPNs (the 5th-LaN and both nc-LaN 1 and 2) present similar axon trajectories, dropping synapses in the lateral horn until reaching the accessory calyx of the mushroom body (Figure 1H–J, Figure 1—figure supplement 3), where they synapse onto Kenyon cells (Eichler et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1H-J and Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and a citation.

claim: PVL09 presents a bifurcated axon with one branch following the other VPNs into the lateral horn and the other branch taking a long looping path below the mushroom body.
source: PVL09 is unique among the VPNs in presenting a bifurcated axon with one branch following the other VPNs into the lateral horn and the other branch taking a long looping path below the mushroom body before coming back to the same region as pOLP (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: All six unique VPNs form synapses in the lateral horn.
source: In summary, all six unique VPNs form synapses in the lateral horn, and three of them (the 5th-LaN, nc-LaN one and nc-LaN 2) synapse onto both the lateral horn and the mushroom body Kenyon cells (Eichler et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: Three VPNs (the 5th-LaN, nc-LaN one and nc-LaN 2) synapse onto both the lateral horn and the mushroom body Kenyon cells.
source: In summary, all six unique VPNs form synapses in the lateral horn, and three of them (the 5th-LaN, nc-LaN one and nc-LaN 2) synapse onto both the lateral horn and the mushroom body Kenyon cells (Eichler et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: The Pdf-LaNs project to a region dorsal and more medial to the lateral horn, similarly as in adult Drosophila.
source: Finally, the Pdf-LaNs, necessary for circadian rhythm, project to a region dorsal and more medial to the lateral horn, similarly as in adult Drosophila (Yasuyama and Meinertzhagen, 2010), where they make few small dyadic synapses from boutons rich in dense-core vesicles (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 3).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 3 and a citation.

claim: Pdf-LaNs boutons contain clear vesicles suggesting that they might co-express a neurotransmitter, which in adult flies has been suggested to be glycine.
source: Pdf-LaNs boutons also contain clear vesicles suggesting that they might co-express a neurotransmitter, which in adult flies has been suggested to be glycine (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; Frenkel et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and a citation.

claim: A pair of serotonergic neurons belonging to the SP2 cluster (named SP2-1) connects to the contralateral LON.
source: A pair of serotonergic neurons belonging to the SP2 cluster (named SP2-1) connects to the contralateral LON, while receiving presynaptic input predominantly in the ipsilateral protocerebrum (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Each sVUM2 innervates both brain hemispheres in a symmetric fashion.
source: Each sVUM2 innervates both brain hemispheres in a symmetric fashion.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the manuscript text.

claim: Each SP2-1 neuron connects to the main VLNs (cha- and glu-lOLPs) as well as to the third-order interneuron VPLN of the contralateral side.
source: Each SP2-1 neuron connects to the main VLNs (cha- and glu-lOLPs) as well as to the third-order interneuron VPLN of the contralateral side (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4D.

claim: The octopaminergic/tyraminergic sVUM2 neurons uniquely synapse onto the two lOLPs but in both hemispheres simultaneously.
source: The octopaminergic/tyraminergic sVUM2 neurons uniquely synapse onto the two lOLPs but in both hemispheres simultaneously (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4E.

claim: The lOLPs form feedback synapses onto the axonal termini of both sVUM2 neurons.
source: In contrast to the SP2-1, the lOLPs form feedback synapses onto the axonal termini of both sVUM2 neurons.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the manuscript text based on connectivity data.

claim: In the current specimen, thirteen PRs were identified in the left hemisphere and sixteen in the right hemisphere.
source: In the current specimen, we identified thirteen PRs in the left hemisphere and sixteen in the right hemisphere.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the manuscript text based on the reconstruction.

claim: Four Rh5-PRs and nine Rh6-PRs were found in the left hemisphere.
source: We found four Rh5-PRs and nine Rh6-PRs in the left hemisphere, and six Rh5-PRs and ten Rh6-PRs in the right hemisphere.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the manuscript text based on the reconstruction.

claim: Six Rh5-PRs and ten Rh6-PRs were found in the right hemisphere.
source: We found four Rh5-PRs and nine Rh6-PRs in the left hemisphere, and six Rh5-PRs and ten Rh6-PRs in the right hemisphere.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the manuscript text based on the reconstruction.

claim: Despite the difference in PRs number, homologous LON interneurons in each hemisphere receive a similar fraction of inputs from PRs.
source: Despite this difference in PRs number, homologous LON interneurons in each hemisphere receive a similar fraction of inputs from PRs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), similarly to olfactory projection interneurons that receive an equivalent fraction of inputs from olfactory receptor neuron despite differences in the numbers of these sensory neurons (Tobin et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and a citation.

claim: A third local-OLP was found in the right brain hemisphere.
source: Interestingly, we found a third local-OLP in the right brain hemisphere.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the manuscript text based on the reconstruction.

claim: Despite the left and right LONs not sharing any interneurons and having a different number of PR and lOLP cells, neurons of the same type cluster closely together in spectral graph analysis.
source: Despite the left and right LONs not sharing any interneurons and having a different number of PR and lOLP cells, we observed that neurons of the same type cluster closely together (Figure 5A), indicating that the circuit structure in which each identified cell is embedded is very similar in the both hemispheres.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5A.

claim: While the number of PRs and VLNs can vary in the larval visual system, the overall circuit architecture is maintained, and in particular the output channels (VPNs) are identical.
source: In conclusion, while the number of PRs and VLNs can vary in the larval visual system, the overall circuit architecture is maintained, and in particular the output channels (VPNs) are identical.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the manuscript text based on the analysis.

claim: Larval PRs lack a clear rhabdomeric structure.
source: Moreover, compared to adult flies PRs, larval PRs lack a clear rhabdomeric structure, do not present intracellular pigment granules and the Bolwig organ is not equipped with focusing optics or other accessory cells (Green et al., 1993; Sprecher et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Larval PRs do not present intracellular pigment granules.
source: Moreover, compared to adult flies PRs, larval PRs lack a clear rhabdomeric structure, do not present intracellular pigment granules and the Bolwig organ is not equipped with focusing optics or other accessory cells (Green et al., 1993; Sprecher et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The Bolwig organ is not equipped with focusing optics or other accessory cells.
source: Moreover, compared to adult flies PRs, larval PRs lack a clear rhabdomeric structure, do not present intracellular pigment granules and the Bolwig organ is not equipped with focusing optics or other accessory cells (Green et al., 1993; Sprecher et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Larval PRs express the main actors of the phototransduction pathway like adult PRs.
source: Nevertheless, larval PRs express the main actors of the phototransduction pathway like adult PRs (Rosenbaum et al., 2011; Mishra et al., 2016; Bernardo-Garcia et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: In the larval visual circuit, there are no significant synaptic connections onto the PRs.
source: However, in the larval visual circuit, we do not observe significant synaptic connections onto the PRs (Figures 2E and 5B), suggesting that the light information encoded by PRs is passed on with no alteration at the level of the first synapse.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figures 2E and 5B.

claim: In dissociated larval Pdf-LaNs, applying acetylcholine increased their calcium response whereas applying glutamate reduced their calcium response.
source: In dissociated larval Pdf-LaNs, it was shown that applying acetylcholine increased their calcium response whereas applying glutamate reduced their calcium response (Wegener et al., 2004; Hamasaka et al., 2007), suggesting that acetylcholine is an excitatory neurotransmitter for these cells whereas glutamate would be inhibitory.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Glutamate has been found to mediate inhibition in the adult fly lobula plate.
source: Therefore, in our view a more favorable scenario is that outputs from cha-lOLP are likely excitatory while the outputs from glu-lOLP are likely inhibitory, similarly as glutamate has been found to mediate inhibition in the adult fly lobula plate (Mauss et al., 2014) and in the antennal lobe (Liu and Wilson, 2013; Berck et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Glutamate has been found to mediate inhibition in the antennal lobe.
source: Therefore, in our view a more favorable scenario is that outputs from cha-lOLP are likely excitatory while the outputs from glu-lOLP are likely inhibitory, similarly as glutamate has been found to mediate inhibition in the adult fly lobula plate (Mauss et al., 2014) and in the antennal lobe (Liu and Wilson, 2013; Berck et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: In the adult fly, the outer R1-6 PRs connect to L1 and L2 interneurons that convey distinct responses to light increment (ON) and decrement (OFF).
source: In the adult fly, the outer R1-6 PRs connect to L1 and L2 interneurons that convey distinct responses to light increment (ON) and decrement (OFF) (Joesch et al., 2010; Clark et al., 2011; Strother et al., 2014; Behnia et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The adult PRs are histaminergic and induce hyperpolarization (inhibition) in both L1 and L2 upon light increment.
source: The adult PRs are histaminergic and induce hyperpolarization (inhibition) in both L1 and L2 upon light increment, followed by a rebound of activity of these two cells upon light decrement (Hardie, 1987; Reiff et al., 2010; Clark et al., 2011); reviewed in Borst and Helmstaedter, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The larval PRs are cholinergic.
source: However, the larval PRs are cholinergic (Yasuyama et al., 1995; Keene et al., 2011) and, at least for the Pdf-LaNs (Yuan et al., 2011), excite their targets activity in response of light.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Each lOLP receives an equivalent number of inputs from each Rh6-PRs (about 20 synapses in average).
source: Another similarity between the two lOLPs and the adult L1 and L2 is that each lOLP receives an equivalent number of inputs from each Rh6-PRs (about 20 synapses in average, Figure 2—source data 1), similarly as adult L1 and L2 receives about 50 inputs from each R1-6 PRs (Meinertzhagen, 1989), suggesting that the information transfer could have a similarly high fidelity.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by source data and a citation.

claim: Adult L1 and L2 receive about 50 inputs from each R1-6 PRs.
source: Another similarity between the two lOLPs and the adult L1 and L2 is that each lOLP receives an equivalent number of inputs from each Rh6-PRs (about 20 synapses in average, Figure 2—source data 1), similarly as adult L1 and L2 receives about 50 inputs from each R1-6 PRs (Meinertzhagen, 1989), suggesting that the information transfer could have a similarly high fidelity.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: In the adult fly, the L1 and L2 are not chemically connected (only electrically).
